$comment: ADR 0125 D1/D8 (+ Amendment 2) · ADR 0126 D5/D7/D10 — the SHARED test vectors
for the two mint-time print derivations.
This file is the single source of truth for BOTH sides of a rule that exists
twice: app.print_source_registers / app.print_source_watermark in SQL, and the
pure client-importable printSourceRegisters / printSourceWatermark in
src/lib/pdf/documents/print-source.ts. A rule duplicated across the SQL/TS
boundary drifts — this is the same hazard CLAUDE.md Architecture Rule 3 answers
for the condition evaluator, and the same answer: one vector file, both
consumers, drift is phase-blocking.
⭐ AND THE MIRROR IS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE OF THIS FILE. ADR 0126 D3 rejects 'both
mechanisms' on the grounds that two computations of one property can disagree
with nothing going red. That rejection stands; it does not bite here SOLELY
because these vectors are what reds. Delete this fixture and the SQL/TS pair
becomes exactly the drift hole D3 refuses.
CONSUMERS (do not add a fourth without updating this list):
1. supabase/tests/vectors/print_source_registers_vectors.psql — GENERATED
from
this file by scripts/gen-print-source-vectors.mjs. ⚠ The extension is
.psql, NOT .sql, and that is deliberate: `supabase test db` runs every
*.sql under supabase/tests/ as its own suite, so a .sql vectors file
would execute standalone (outside 344's plan) and fail. It is pulled in
by `\ir` from 344 instead. pgTAP cannot read a JSON
file at test time (it runs INSIDE the database; pg_read_file needs superuser
AND a container-visible path), so the vectors are compiled to SQL at build
time instead. The generated file carries a sourceSha256 header.
2. src/lib/queries/print-source-vectors.test.ts (backend-owned) — the SYNC
GUARD. Asserts the generated .sql is in sync with this file via that hash,
so editing either one alone REDS `npm run test`. It deliberately tests
NEITHER predicate: a parity test that also owned the semantics could go
green by agreeing with itself.
3. src/lib/pdf-mint/print-source-vectors.test.ts (frontend-owned) — the TS
SEMANTICS. ⚠ Deliberately NOT colocated with its subject: `src/lib/pdf/**`
is pure (ADR 0104 D14) and eslint BANS every path shape reaching
`src/lib/queries` — where this fixture lives — so a colocated suite could
not read it, and dodging the ban would weaken a gate to move a test.
4. the pgTAP suite over the SQL predicates (backend-owned), which loads the
generated .sql from consumer 1.
INPUT SHAPE (0126 round 2 + the two disposal conjuncts). A vector is
(kind, status, correction_open, phase_voided, meeting_disposed, case_disposed)
-> (registers, watermark). All four flags default FALSE when absent, and each
is KIND-SCOPED — every predicate must IGNORE a flag outside its kind. That
ignoring is PINNED by the cross-kind rows below, not left to the comment.
correction_open  (form_response only) = an open, still-rejectable correction
request exists whose draft_response_id is this response — operationally:
case_correction_requests.status in ('resubmitted','under_review'), the
exact set reject_correction accepts (0126 D10). In requested/in_progress/
rejected the draft is not submitted; in approved/withdrawn the request is
closed (both measured terminal).
phase_voided     (form_response only) = the attached case_phase has status
'voided' (0126 D10; measured terminal — activate_phase refuses anything
but 'pending', HC019; a future un-void door re-opens the question,
standing rule in 0126's method note).
meeting_disposed (meeting only) = meetings.phi_disposed_at is not null.
dispose_meeting_minutes nulls minutes_md and redacts the agenda text
WITHOUT touching status or revision, so a registered print would pin a
content_hash for content that no longer exists and would read 'atual'
forever. Measured constructible: on a signed meeting with ZERO agenda
items the door succeeds (with agenda items guard_meeting_child_lock
refuses it outright — a separate, filed defect).
case_disposed    (case only, PDF·P3 / ADR 0144 D3+D10) =
cases.phi_disposed_at is not null. The case analogue of
meeting_disposed and the STRONGER of the two: dispose_case_phi does not
null one column, it GUTS the dossier — DELETES patient_identifiers and
the phases' answers, nulls case_narratives.body_md and
case_interviews.summary_md, redacts case_events.body/.title, the
interview-subject notes, cases.label, documents.title/.description and
meeting_cases.summary/.decision — while leaving cases.status UNTOUCHED.
So the status term alone cannot see it, exactly as for meetings.
⚠ THE CASE STATUS SET IS not_started / in_review / pending / completed /
cancelled — there is NO 'open'. An earlier placeholder vector in this file used
'open', a value cases.status cannot hold; it asserted the fail-closed ELSE
under a label that read like a real lifecycle state. It is replaced below by
the full 5 x {disposed, not} cross-product (ADR 0144 D14).
⭐ THE CASE KIND DIVERGES FROM THE MEETING KIND AT `cancelled`, ON PURPOSE.
A cancelled MEETING does not register (no minutes to pin); a cancelled CASE
DOES — it has a complete process record worth attesting to, and it is
terminal-FOREVER (reopen_case refuses it with HC0M8, and cancel_case raises
HC025 on any terminal so completed->cancelled is unconstructible), which makes
its currency claim unconditional. It is the STRONGER of the two terminal
states here and the excluded one there. Anyone 'harmonising' the two kinds
reds on these rows, which is the point.
TWO AXES, DECLARED SEPARATELY — that separation is D8's point, not ceremony.
registers  = is this source LOCKED, such that printing it yields a REGISTERED
emission (permanent, hash-pinned, QR-verifiable)?
watermark  = is the CONTENT final ('final'), or not yet ('draft')?
For form_response the two axes RE-coincide — 0125 Amendment 2 refined the
watermark in tandem with 0126 D5/D10's lock refinement; the coincidence is
recorded, not exploited. For meeting they SEPARATE at in_signature, which is
exactly why a single predicate looked sufficient until meetings were examined.
⚠ THE DISPOSAL CONJUNCT MOVES BOTH MEETING AXES IN TANDEM, and it has to.
Registration alone would make a signed+disposed meeting registers=false while
the watermark still read 'final' from the status — the FORBIDDEN fourth cell,
reached. This is 0125 Amendment 2's shape recurring for the meeting kind, and
it takes Amendment 2's answer. ⛔ meetingWatermarkFor is STILL not changed
(0125 D1): it stays a pure function of status, and the disposal term composes
ON TOP of it inside printSourceWatermark — which is also why the renderer must
take its mark from printSourceWatermark, not from meetingWatermarkFor directly.
⚠ NOT COVERED HERE: currency/head (0126 D2/D8/D9). It reads chain, pointer and
revision state that a stateless vector cannot carry; its coverage is the
two-sided keystones 0126's Consequences demand. Do not read this suite as
covering it. ⭐ And note the BOUND currency actually carries: it answers 'is
this print of the current REVISION of the source record', NOT 'would a
re-render be byte-identical'. For meetings those differ by construction —
sign_meeting changes the rendered footer and action-item progress renders live
— so currency is not, and cannot be, a content-integrity guarantee.
INVARIANT (ADR 0125 D5, the fourth cell): there is no vector with
watermark='final' AND registers=false. A FINAL page carrying the prévia footer
would be a page the platform disclaims. The invariant SURVIVES 0126 D5/D10 and
the disposal conjunct because the watermark moved in tandem BOTH times — keyed
on status alone, the correction_open row and the meeting_disposed row below
would each be its counterexample. Every consumer asserts it over these rows
rather than reasoning about it.

vectors.note: Ephemeral prévia. D2 amends ADR 0104 D7 item 4: completeness gates REGISTRATION, not PRINTING — the user still gets paper, it just never enters the registry.
Both axes turn together here — and the DEFAULTS matter: no open correction, no voided phase. This row is the differential that stops a fail-closed stub from passing the two refined rows below.

⭐ 0126 D5 + 0125 Amendment 2 — the tandem move. A submitted draft of an open, still-rejectable correction is NOT a lock point: reject_correction can walk it back to in_progress (the corridor that raised HC069 — 0125 Amendment 1 §A). It prints as a RASCUNHO prévia ('not settled'). Keyed on `submitted` alone, THIS row is the reachable fourth cell.
The rejected-and-walked-back draft. Same output as the plain in_progress row ON PURPOSE — the predicate must fail closed here with or without the correction flag.

0126 D10. approve_correction(kind='void') annuls the PHASE without touching the response — the request closes, so without this conjunct both currency conjuncts read true again and annulled paper stays 'current' forever. The void door sat one column outside round 1's sweep; see the standing read-set rule.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE, pinned rather than commented: meeting_disposed is a MEETING flag and both form_response arms must ignore it. Without this row 'the flags are kind-scoped' is an assertion no test makes — and a predicate that read it here would silently refuse to register every submitted response the moment the flag was wired up.
Freely editable and freely deletable.

Still deletable — app.guard_meeting_status does NOT refuse a DELETE at held. Ephemeral. ⚠ held is also where a REOPENED ata lands (0126 D9): its prior registered print exists and loses currency via the revision mismatch, not via anything this vector can see.

⭐ THE SEPARATING CASE. An ata circulating for signature is a document of record — undeletable from this moment (guard_meeting_status refuses DELETE) and it is what the committee is being asked to attest to. It REGISTERS, stamped RASCUNHO: permanent and QR-verifiable, honestly marked not-yet-approved. meetingWatermarkFor is NOT changed.

Re-minting here supersedes the in_signature print, so the circulated draft survives as SUBSTITUÍDO with its own hash — the accreditation answer to 'show me the minutes circulated on the 12th'. ⚠ 0126 D9 justified this staying current with '(same revision, content identical)'; the second half is FALSE — sign_meeting writes meeting_signatures, which the template renders as the footer, and that table carries no child lock. The conclusion stands, the mechanism does not.
Terminal.

⛔ LOCKED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERING — the ONE place the registering set is a strict subset of the lock set (D1). guard_meeting_status refuses a DELETE at cancelled, so a name like 'is_locked' would have to return TRUE here and would be a lie about what the predicate decides. The lock exists to preserve the audit trail of a cancellation, not because an ata of record was produced: there are no minutes to pin. A decision, not an oversight — and it carries its own keystone.

⭐⭐ THE DISPOSAL CONJUNCT, and the row that carries BOTH axes. dispose_meeting_minutes nulls minutes_md and redacts the agenda WITHOUT touching status or revision — the meeting analogue of D10's voided phase: a deliberate, authorized, terminal annulment of the record's content. Registration drops, so currency falls out of D2's first conjunct for free, and no disposed meeting can mint NEW registered paper for a record the platform was just obligated to destroy. ⛔ The watermark MUST drop with it: keyed on status alone this row is registers=false + watermark='final', the forbidden fourth cell, reached.

The disposal conjunct ISOLATED from the tandem watermark move: at in_signature the watermark is already 'draft', so only `registers` changes between this row and the plain in_signature row above. Without it, a predicate that dropped ONLY the watermark on disposal would still pass the signed+disposed row.
Disposal beats the terminal status too — the conjunct is on the state, not on how the meeting got there.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE, the mirror of the form_response row above: correction_open and phase_voided are FORM_RESPONSE flags and both meeting arms must ignore them. This is the row that reds if someone 'simplifies' the dispatch into a single flag-reading predicate shared across kinds.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE for the NEW flag: case_disposed is a CASE fact and both form_response arms must ignore it. Added with the flag itself — a new flag that no existing kind's vectors carry is a flag whose kind-scoping is untested for those kinds (see 'a new door must inherit every sibling arm').

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE for the NEW flag, meeting side. Deliberately paired with the row above: a predicate that read case_disposed globally would refuse to register every signed ata for a disposed case, which is nonsense the type system cannot prevent.
PDF·P3 / ADR 0144 D3. Non-terminal ⇒ freely editable ⇒ ephemeral prévia, never a registered emission. The case has not begun; there is nothing to attest to.

Disposal on a non-terminal case changes nothing about EITHER axis — both were already false. The row exists so the cross-product has no hole: absence here would let a predicate that INVERTED the disposal conjunct pass on every non-terminal row.
Under active committee work — the most editable state there is.
As above.

⚠ 'pending' is NOT terminal despite sounding settled — it is where a REOPENED case lands (reopen_case moves completed -> pending). A print taken before the reopen keeps existing; it loses currency through the D15 revision bump, which no stateless vector can see.
As above.

⭐ THE LOCK POINT. Both axes turn together, and the DEFAULTS matter: not disposed. This row is the differential that stops a fail-closed stub from passing every other case row — without it, 'return false' satisfies 9 of the 10.

⭐⭐ THE DISPOSAL CONJUNCT, and the row that carries BOTH axes for the case kind. dispose_case_phi guts the rendered content while leaving status UNTOUCHED, so neither the status term nor the D15 revision match can see it. ⛔ The watermark MUST drop in tandem: keyed on status alone this row is registers=false + watermark='final' — ADR 0125 D5's forbidden FOURTH CELL, reached. Third kind, same shape, same answer.

⭐ REGISTERS — the deliberate DIVERGENCE from the meeting kind, where cancelled is the one excluded state. Terminal-forever (HC0M8: reopen_case refuses cancelled), so the currency claim is unconditional; and a cancelled case, unlike a cancelled meeting, has a complete process record worth attesting to. This is the row that reds if someone 'harmonises' the two kinds.
Disposal beats the terminal status here too — the conjunct is on the state, not on how the case got there. Mirrors the meeting distributed+disposed row.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE, isolated: correction_open is a FORM_RESPONSE flag. Deliberately its OWN row rather than folded into a set-everything row — a combined row proves some flag is ignored but not WHICH, and a predicate leaking exactly one of the three would still pass it.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE, isolated: phase_voided is a FORM_RESPONSE flag. ⚠ This one is the most tempting to leak — a case OWNS the phases whose voiding sets it, so 'a voided phase should stop the dossier registering' reads plausible. It must not: the dossier renders every phase including voided ones, and the case's own lock point is its status.

⭐ CROSS-KIND IGNORE, isolated: meeting_disposed is a MEETING flag. ⚠ Also tempting to leak, and for a sharper reason — a case IS discussed in meetings and the dossier renders meeting_cases rows. A disposed MEETING still must not suppress the CASE's registration; the case's own disposal flag is the only one that does.
D8, as above (P4).

ELSE_FAIL_CLOSED — an unhandled kind is EPHEMERAL, mirroring app.can_view_printed_document's fail-closed ELSE. A new printable kind that forgets its arm fails shut rather than quietly registering everything.

The fail-closed ELSE with EVERY flag set and a status that registers for a known kind — so the ELSE is pinned as unreachable-by-flags, not merely untested. A dispatch that fell through to a shared flag-reading tail would answer differently here. ⚠ case_disposed added with the flag: a fail-closed row that omits the newest flag stops being 'every flag' the moment one is added, and nothing would say so.
